correctness.rationale: The exact transition identity M^8=I+3B and eight coefficients c_r are reconstructed by multiplication. Binomial lifting holds modulo 3^(j+2) for every integer j≥0; for five coefficients units modulo three, the leading term of a_(8t+r)−a_(8s+r) has exact valuation 1+ν3(t−s). An injective map from 3^(k−1) index residues to one 3-mod class is automatically bijective; matrix periodicity plus the branch identity establishes the least period. All conclusions are universal algebraic deductions. Standalone checks cover 26,240 recurrence terms and 7,425 exact-integer index pairs. No unproved asymptotic step is required.

originality.rationale: Guadalupe (2021) and Ismail–Rihane–Anwar (2022) prove fixed-target three-adic valuation formulas for the same recurrence, while the assessed statement is a five-branch pairwise isometry valid for arbitrary pairs of indices, with all-power residue-class bijections and uniquely represented 2-mod-3 residues. The general second-order residue-completeness results of Lang and Lang do not contain this third-order recurrence. OEIS lists periods and is not credited as a new result. Actual research-record and literature searches returned related recurrences but no covering theorem. This supports provisional originality, not an exhaustive priority guarantee; full 2015 Narayana-mod-prime text was unavailable.

value.rationale: A longstanding classical third-order recurrence has a natural but nonuniform modular orbit. The classification shows exact all-power surjectivity and a sharp singleton-vs-multiple-fibre dichotomy, generated by five explicit three-adic isometries. This answers a precise, structurally motivated residue-completeness and multiplicity question rather than tabulating a chosen cutoff. It extends the type of valuation restrictions already studied in 2021–22 without claiming those restrictions anew.
